Adobe is rolling out a limited test today, giving some Project Indigo users access to multiple generative AI-powered photo editing tools. Details below.

Adobe adds experimental AI Playground to Project Indigo

More than a year ago, Adobe announced Project Indigo, a free experimental camera app for iPhone that offers full manual controls and a more natural, DSLR-like approach to computational photography.

In April last year, Adobe expanded Project Indigo to select iPads and the iPhone 17e, with that update also adding new grid views, a photo culling feature, and a number of stability and image quality improvements.

Today Adobe is once again expanding Project Indigo's toolset with the addition of AI Playground. Adobe says:

If you are one of the users invited to try the Project Indigo AI Playground, you will see a launch screen inviting you to take part in the experiment. Adobe stresses that this is voluntary, and for users who choose to take part, the company will only collect keypress records during your use of the Playground.

Meaning Adobe "will not look at your prompts or images, nor upload them to【its】servers or use them to train AI models." The company adds that "since sign-in is not required, the analytics data we collect is anonymous."

Once users are granted access to the Project Indigo AI Playground, they will see four new sections. Here is what Adobe says about each feature, with examples:

Adobe says it is currently using Google's Nano Banana model, and that the output images will only be standard dynamic range (SDR) even when users shoot in high dynamic range (HDR). To address this, the company "built a custom machine learning model specifically to post-process the SDR images returned by Nano Banana and bump them back up to HDR." Adobe adds that this process is not perfect and relies heavily on the quality of Nano Banana's output.

Finally, the company explains that the Project Indigo AI Playground features only work on images captured within the app. In other words, if you import photos from elsewhere, the magic button that opens the AI Playground will be greyed out and unavailable.
